we need to consider the ways in which individuals manage their disclosure in social network sites (SNSs), and that we need to understand that the management of disclosure is not an individual task, but rather an interpersonal process.

we found that people use a range of strategies to cope with the disclosure of information about them on social network services, and that they also use collaborative strategies to manage the disclosure of information by others about them.
people are dependent on others' disclosure in SNS, and that they use collaborative strategies to manage disclosure.

how to design for a more equitable distribution of the workload needed for managing disclosure in SNS.
understanding how people manage disclosure online, in particular how they cope with the challenges of privacy in social network services.
understanding and designing for a new type of social interaction in which the management of disclosure is shared between people.

the management of disclosure is not only an individual process but also an interpersonal one.
the management of disclosure in online social networks requires both individual as well as collaborative strategies.
the framework and design solutions proposed are supportive of collaborative and preventative strategies in boundary regulation and facilitate the management of online disclosure in SNS.

people need to be able to take back control in the disclosure of personal information.

the management of disclosure in online social networks is a collective responsibility that can be supported by design.
